dedupe_keys.name: uk digital switchover of terrestrial television and the nao review 2008 to 2012

description: This investment and policy case covers the United Kingdom's region-by-region switch from analogue to digital terrestrial television between 2008 and 2012, which also cleared the 800 MHz band for 4G mobile, and the National Audit Office's value-for-money review of the preparations. The NAO report of 27 February 2008 set out the government's estimate that the programme would cost the economy 4.6 billion pounds, 3.8 billion of it for consumers converting or replacing sets, against benefits of 6.3 billion pounds from wider coverage and new services. It noted that 85 per cent of households already used digital TV on their main set but that 26 million other sets still needed converting, that nearly a third of licence payers did not understand switchover, and that a help scheme for older and disabled people, run by the BBC, had up to 603 million pounds ring-fenced. It urged coordinated work across government and delivery bodies and better consumer information. A separate NAO report looked at the BBC's preparedness. Coverage: the whole UK, 2008 to 2012. Format and access: NAO report web page and PDF, free. Caveats: the review is ex-ante; an ex-post evaluation was not read. Simulation uses: cost-benefit appraisal of network technology transitions, transmitter network re-engineering and spectrum reallocation planning. Related records: Norway's FM switch-off is a comparable radio transition; the Ofcom broadcast transmitter parameters describe today's network.
